newsitem.title: LEBANON: Beirut's Solidere down after two-week surge.
newsitem.headline: Beirut's Solidere down after two-week surge.

text.p: Solidere fell slightly in sharply increased turnover on Wednesday after a two-week surge to the highest levels in two years on the Beirut Stock Exchange.
Bank shares traded at record highs in strong demand.
Solidere A shares fell to $13.125 from $13.75 while B shares fell to $13.50 from $13.75. The shares climbed from $10.75 on July 1 while B shares traded at $10.875 on that day.
BSE turnover rose 87.3 percent to 832,541 shares for a value of $11,455,359 from Tuesday's 444,581 shares for a value of $6,179,930.
Turnover in Solidere rose sharply to 752,491 shares from 338,971 a day earlier.
Bank shares traded in strong demand.
Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce hit a high of $21.5 from $20.75. Bank of Beirut hit $4.6875 from $4.625. Banque Audi recaught its previously-touched high of $28.5, up from $28 a day earlier.
The LIBX bank index rose 2.25 percent to 185.07. The BLOM general index fell 2.7 percent to 1128.76. The LISPI general index rose 0.02 percent to hit 95.73.
There was no trade in the four listed industrial firms: Ciment Libanaise, Ciments Blanc, Eternit and Uniceramic.
